props.heading: A clearer starting point for student-support conversations.
props.subheading: Aether Student Resiliency Framework • Public resource
props.description: Aether is a research-informed framework for connecting wellbeing, learning habits, and clearer support pathways. It is a discussion and planning artifact—not a clinical tool, diagnostic system, or validated intervention study.

props.heading: Three connected areas, one responsible conversation.
props.description: The framework makes room for wellbeing, learning habits, and support pathways without reducing a student to a score or a diagnosis.

features.title: Wellbeing context
features.description: Make space for the conditions that affect how a student is able to learn, participate, and ask for help.

features.title: Learning habits
features.description: Identify practical routines, friction points, and supports that can make learning feel more navigable.

features.title: Support pathways
features.description: Clarify who can help, what an appropriate next step is, and when qualified adult or professional guidance is needed.

props.heading: Designed to be useful, explicit, and reviewable.
props.description: The public record makes it possible to see the question, the proposed method, and the limits of the current artifact before deciding whether a conversation is worthwhile.

items.title: Aether Student Resiliency Framework
items.description: A documented model for communicating a proposed student-support approach to mentors, educators, and potential collaborators.
items.question: How can a framework make wellbeing, learning habits, and intervention pathways easier to discuss and improve?
items.method: Define needs, map support touchpoints, identify meaningful signals, and turn the work into a usable, reviewable artifact.
items.evidence: Framework PDF, public portfolio documentation, and an open support-center workflow.
items.outcome: A shared starting point for feedback and ethical pilot-scoping discussions.
items.limitation: This is not a validated clinical, therapeutic, or school-wide intervention study. It should not replace qualified professional support.
items.nextStep: Gather structured reviewer feedback and define an ethical, measurable pilot scope with an appropriate supervising adult or institution.

props.heading: Framework questions
props.description: Short answers before you download, share, or discuss the framework.

faqs.question: Who is this framework for?
faqs.answer: It is intended as a discussion and planning resource for students, educators, mentors, and community collaborators who are considering clearer student-support pathways.

faqs.question: Is Aether a clinical or diagnostic tool?
faqs.answer: No. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace qualified medical, mental-health, school, or safeguarding professionals.

faqs.question: Can a school adopt it as an intervention?
faqs.answer: Not on the basis of this public artifact alone. Any real-world pilot should have appropriate adult supervision, institutional review, safeguarding, and measurable evaluation.

props.heading: Read the framework. Bring a thoughtful question.
props.description: If you are an educator, mentor, or community partner, begin with the public artifact and then share the context needed for a responsible conversation.
